summary: The main article describes an NHC and visible light co-catalyzed 1,4-sulfonylacylation of 1,3-enynes to produce tetrasubstituted allenyl ketones. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope schemes for enynes, sulfonyl sources, and acyl fluorides, as well as mechanistic studies and derivatization reactions.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Radical C -C bond formation based on BI-derived ketyltype radicals.
items.description: This scheme compares previous radical cross-couplings based on BI-evolved ketyl radicals with the current work's 1,4-sulfonylacylation of 1,3-enynes.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Conditions optimization a , b
items.description: This table details the optimization of reaction conditions, including screening of photocatalysts, NHC catalysts, and solvents to maximize the yield of product 4.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Substrate scope for 1,4-sulfonylacylation of 1,3-enynes. a , b
items.description: This scheme illustrates the broad substrate scope for 1,3-enynes, sulfonyl radical sources, and acyl fluorides, including late-stage functionalization of natural product derivatives.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Attempts at asymmetric 1,4-sulfonylacylation of 1,3enynes.
items.description: This scheme shows the results of using chiral NHC catalysts, which yielded products with low enantioselectivity.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Large-scale synthesis and derivatization reactions.
items.description: This scheme demonstrates a 2.0 mmol scale synthesis and various chemical transformations of the allenyl ketone product, such as reduction and Nazarov cyclization.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Mechanism investigation.
items.description: This scheme presents control experiments, radical trapping with TEMPO, and the use of an acyl azolium intermediate to probe the reaction mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 6
items.caption: Stern -Volmer quenching studies.
items.description: This item refers to the luminescence quenching studies used to identify the oxidative quenching process between the photocatalyst and the acyl azolium ion.

items.heading: Scheme 7
items.caption: Proposed catalytic cycle.
items.description: This scheme outlines the proposed dual catalytic cycle involving NHC and photoredox catalysis, highlighting the radical-radical cross-coupling step.
